note: Every economic corridor India is a party to, international and national. Each entry gives when the corridor was begun — many before 2014 — what has happened since, and its status as last reported, with the sources it was checked against. Routes are drawn through their main nodes, not surveyed alignments.

corridors.name: India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)
corridors.startedNote: MoU signed on 9 September 2023 at the G20 summit in New Delhi.
corridors.statusNote: A framework, largely unbuilt. India's foreign minister said in February 2026 it was progressing 'but not at the pace initially expected', slowed by war in West Asia.
facts: Sea from India's west coast to the UAE, rail across the Arabian peninsula to the Mediterranean, sea again to Europe.
Israel and Jordan are on the planned route; sources differ on whether they signed the 2023 MoU.

corridors.name: International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC)
corridors.startedNote: Agreed by India, Iran and Russia in 2000.
corridors.statusNote: Cargo moves on parts of the route; missing rail links in Iran and sanctions limit it. The Commerce Ministry estimates freight could become 30% cheaper and 40% faster once the network is complete.
facts: About 7,200 km, Mumbai to Moscow via Iran and the Caspian.
Bypasses the Suez Canal route to Russia and Europe.

corridors.name: Chabahar port (Shahid Beheshti terminal)
corridors.mode: Port and road to Afghanistan and Central Asia
corridors.startedNote: India–Iran–Afghanistan transit agreement, 2016; a ten-year operating contract signed on 13 May 2024.
corridors.statusNote: India Ports Global operates the terminal under the 2024 contract, committing $120 million, with a $250 million credit line for Iranian transport links. US sanctions on Iran have slowed it throughout.
facts: India's route to Afghanistan and Central Asia that avoids Pakistan.
Can feed the INSTC's eastern branch.

corridors.name: Chennai–Vladivostok Eastern Maritime Corridor
corridors.startedNote: Agreed at the Eastern Economic Forum, Vladivostok, in 2019.
corridors.statusNote: Declared operational in November 2024; ships carrying crude oil, metals and textiles had begun arriving at Indian ports.
facts: The government estimates it saves up to 16 days against the route via Europe.

corridors.name: India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway
corridors.startedNote: Proposed at a trilateral ministerial meeting in 2002.
corridors.statusNote: About 1,360 km from Moreh to Mae Sot. India's sections in Myanmar — the 120 km Kalewa–Yagyi road and 69 bridges — have moved 'in fits and starts' amid Myanmar's civil war; both governments pledged in June 2026 to speed it up.
facts: Would link India's Northeast to Southeast Asia by road.

corridors.name: Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project
corridors.statusNote: Sittwe port, the Paletwa river terminal and dredging are complete; the road from Paletwa to the Mizoram border is not, in a part of Rakhine state where fighting continues.
facts: Kolkata to Sittwe by sea, up the Kaladan river to Paletwa, by road to Mizoram.
About $484 million in all, of which the Paletwa road is about $324 million.

corridors.name: BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement
corridors.statusNote: Bhutan stepped back in 2017; Bangladesh, India and Nepal later finalised the protocol to operate it among themselves. Bhutan says it remains committed. Not in force across all four.
facts: Would let passenger and cargo vehicles cross the four countries' borders without trans-shipment.

corridors.name: Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor
corridors.startedNote: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation set up in 2006.
corridors.statusNote: All 1,337 km, Ludhiana to Sonnagar, complete by February 2024.
facts: Moves freight off the passenger network on the busiest route in the country.

corridors.name: Western Dedicated Freight Corridor
corridors.startedNote: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation set up in 2006.
corridors.statusNote: 1,506 km, Jawaharlal Nehru Port to Dadri. Reported 93.2% complete in 2024–25 with the last stretch to the port targeted for late 2025; final completion not confirmed from two sources.
facts: Links the western ports to the north Indian plains for container freight.

corridors.name: Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail
corridors.statusNote: 508 km. By September 2026, 371 km of viaduct was built and physical progress put at 62.16%. The first section, Surat–Bilimora, is targeted for August 2027 — five years after the original date — and the full line for the end of 2029.
facts: India's first high-speed line, with Japanese Shinkansen technology.

corridors.name: Delhi–Mumbai Expressway
corridors.startedNote: Foundation stone laid in 2019; first due in 2024.
corridors.statusNote: About 1,350 km. The minister put it at 75–80% complete in July 2026; three Gujarat packages are now due in March 2028.
facts: The longest of the access-controlled corridors built since 2014.

corridors.name: National Industrial Corridor Development Programme
corridors.startedNote: The Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor, the first, was begun with Japan in 2007.
corridors.statusNote: 11 corridors and 32 projects in four phases. Twelve more industrial smart cities in ten states were approved on 28 August 2024, with ₹28,602 crore.
facts: The government's estimate for the twelve new cities: ₹1.5 lakh crore of investment potential and 10 lakh direct jobs — projections, not results.

corridors.name: Defence industrial corridors (Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu)
corridors.statusNote: Investment grounded is a fraction of what was committed — see the series below, from this site's record.
facts: Eleven nodes, from Agra and Lucknow to Chennai and Hosur.

logistics.title: World Bank Logistics Performance Index: India's rank
logistics.note: Lower is better. The index skipped 2020 and was restructured for 2023, so the last step is not strictly like-for-like; India's best rank was 35th, in 2016.
